key.name: peek-px
key.description: How much of a parked window stays visible at the screen edge. 0 pushes it fully out of sight.

key.name: animation-duration
key.description: How long windows take to leave for the edge and to come back.

key.name: easing
key.description: The easing curve windows follow on their way to the edge and back.

key.name: swipe-up-action
key.description: Upstream has no upward gesture and leaves the swipe to GNOME's overview. 'mission-control' spreads the workspace's windows out to be picked from instead. macOS opens Mission Control by swiping up with four fingers.

key.name: swipe-down-action
key.description: 'show-desktop' parks the windows at the screen edge, which is what this extension has always done. 'app-expose' spreads only the focused application's windows, as macOS does when swiping down with four fingers.

key.name: pinch-opens-launchpad
key.summary: Pinching in on a bare desktop opens the app grid
key.description: With nothing parked, a four-finger pinch has nothing to bring back. macOS opens Launchpad on that gesture. This asks the overview for its app grid, which a launcher extension replacing the grid will answer instead.

key.name: suppress-other-vertical-swipes
key.summary: Swallow vertical swipes with a different finger count
key.description: GNOME's overview answers to any vertical swipe of three or more fingers, so raising swipe-finger-count leaves the lower counts still opening it. This consumes those. Horizontal swipes are never touched, so switching workspaces keeps working.

key.name: launcher-extension-uuid
key.summary: Launcher extension a spread should dismiss
key.description: UUID of an extension publishing an isLauncherOpen() method. While it reports itself open, a spread closes it instead of parking the windows behind it -- the gesture macOS dismisses Launchpad with. Empty disables this.

key.name: swipe-finger-count
key.summary: Fingers on the pad for the vertical swipe
key.description: How many fingers the show-desktop swipe wants. GNOME's own overview gesture answers to any swipe of three or more, so raising this to 4 moves out of its way. macOS puts its navigation gestures on four fingers and leaves three free.

key.name: pinch-show-scale
key.description: How far a four-finger spread opens between the windows sitting at home and being fully parked. Larger means the same finger movement moves the windows less.

key.name: pinch-restore-scale
key.description: How far a four-finger pinch closes between the windows being parked and back at home. Smaller means the same finger movement moves the windows less.

key.name: pinch-commit-progress
key.summary: How far to travel before letting go finishes the gesture
key.description: The fraction of the spread or pinch that has to be covered for releasing the fingers to complete it rather than put the windows back. Deliberately separate from the travel keys, so the motion can be slowed without also making it harder to commit to. Lower commits sooner.

key.name: mission-control-toggle
key.description: Spread the windows of the current workspace out to be picked from, the way Mission Control does. macOS uses Control+Up for this.

key.name: show-desktop-toggle
key.description: Park every window at the screen edge, and bring them back when pressed again. The same toggle the gestures and a click on empty desktop use. macOS shows the desktop with Command and the Mission Control key.

key.name: grid-padding-px
key.description: Space between the tiled windows and around the edge of the screen.
